title: SVG Ingestion, AST Parsing & Path Equalization Architecture

blocks.content: Engineering notebook from `docs/SVG_SYSTEM_AND_PATH_EQUALIZATION_ARCHITECTURE.md`. This archive preserves the project’s original rationale, equations, performance reports and illustrative code. Historical paths, API names, claims and sketches can differ from the current engine. For copy-ready programs use the guides and demos; for current callable signatures use the source-derived API. Performance figures here describe reported experiments, not guaranteed frame rates.

blocks.text: Original document: [docs/SVG_SYSTEM_AND_PATH_EQUALIZATION_ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/docs/SVG_SYSTEM_AND_PATH_EQUALIZATION_ARCHITECTURE.md). See [current limitations](/limitations) for concrete compatibility notes.

Importing vector artwork (icons, logos, diagrams, mathematical illustrations) from design software (Illustrator, Inkscape, Figma) requires a robust conversion pipeline from standard XML SVG markup into Retiam's WebGPU vector representations ([`Path`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/2d/Path.ts) and [`VectorEntity`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/VectorEntity.ts)).
Retiam provides two specialized SVG entities and a mathematical contour equalizer:

items: **[`SVG`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/composites/svg/SVG.ts)**: High-level composite entity that ingests full SVG documents, parses the document Object Model (DOM) tree via `svg-parser`, resolves cascading CSS classes and inline styles, expands `<defs>` / `<use>` templates, and preserves layer hierarchies as a tree of WebGPU entities.

**[`SVGPath`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/composites/svg/SVGPath.ts)**: Single-entity path extractor that parses SVG path `d="..."` attribute commands and collapses all contours into a unified vertex buffer for maximum GPU rendering throughput.

**[`PathEqualizer`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/utils/PathEqualizer.ts)**: Algorithmic utility that balances contour counts, segment counts, and arc-length vertex distributions between two disparate vector shapes to enable continuous, artifact-free topological morphing.

items: **Pass 1 (`findDefs`)**: Recursively traverses the AST, indexing all nodes bearing an `id` attribute into `rawDefsMap`. This allows later `<use href="#id">` references to be resolved instantaneously without linear tree searches.

items.text: **Pass 2 (`decodeNode`)**: Traverses structural elements (`<svg>`, `<g>`), applying affine transformation matrices and styling cascades to child leaves:
children: `<path>`: Parses SVG path grammar into Bézier contours.
`<rect>`: Converts `x`, `y`, `width`, `height`, and optional rounded corners `rx`, `ry` into a [`Rect`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/2d/Rect.ts).

`<circle>` & `<ellipse>`: Maps center coordinates $(c_x, c_y)$ and radii $(r_x, r_y)$ to [`Circle`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/2d/Circle.ts) and [`Ellipse`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/2d/Ellipse.ts).
`<polygon>` & `<polyline>`: Parses space/comma-separated coordinate strings into contiguous contour vertex arrays.
`<use>`: Resolves target templates from `rawDefsMap`, clones the template subtree, and applies the instance's local `x`, `y`, and `transform` attributes.

blocks.text: SVG styles originate from four competing sources. Retiam resolves them according to standard CSS specificity:

items: **Default Presentation**: SVG standards dictate a default black fill (`#000000`) and transparent stroke. Setting `ignoreSvgDefaults: true` overrides this behavior, permitting inherited scene/parent styling to cascade down.
**Document Stylesheets**: `<style>` tag declarations are parsed into a scoped `classStyles: Map<string, Record<string, string>>`.
**Inline Styles**: Declarations inside `style="..."` take highest precedence.

blocks.text: Transforms (`matrix`, `translate`, `scale`, `rotate`, `skewX`, `skewY`) are parsed via regular expressions into 3x3 matrices ([`Mat3`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/math/vector/Mat3.ts)) and multiplied cumulatively down the entity hierarchy.

While [`SVG`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/composites/svg/SVG.ts) builds an explicit scene graph of nested entities, [`SVGPath`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/composites/svg/SVGPath.ts) flattens all contours into a single [`Path`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/2d/Path.ts) entity.
The path interpreter evaluates the complete SVG path specification:

items: **MoveTo (`M`, `m`)**: Terminates current contour and establishes a new start vertex.
**Cubic Bézier (`C`, `c`, `S`, `s`)**: Emits cubic Bézier curves, automatically reflecting the control point for smooth continuation (`S`).
**Quadratic Bézier (`Q`, `q`, `T`, `t`)**: Evaluates quadratic control points with smooth tangent reflection (`T`).

**Elliptical Arc (`A`, `a`)**: Converts SVG endpoint arc parameterization $(r_x, r_y, \phi, f_A, f_S, x_2, y_2)$ into center parameterization $(\theta_1, \Delta\theta)$ and subdivides the arc into cubic Bézier segments ($\Delta\theta \le \pi / 2$).
**ClosePath (`Z`, `z`)**: Closes the contour back to the first vertex.

blocks.text: Morphing between two distinct vector graphics (e.g. morphing an SVG checkmark into an SVG cross) requires the source and target geometries to share **identical contour counts** and **identical vertex counts per contour**:

1 contour, 40 vertices"] --> B["Contour balancing
Add a degenerate zero-area contour: 1 → 2"] T["Target SVG
2 contours, 100 vertices"] --> B B --> R["Arc-length resampling
Equal segment density: 120 vertices each"] R --> A["Winding and alignment
Minimize summed squared vertex travel distance"]

items: **Contour Count Balancing**: If $n < m$, degenerate zero-length / zero-area contours located at the geometric center of the shape are inserted into $C_A$ until $|C_A| = |C_B|$.

**Arc-Length Resampling**: For matching contour pairs $(c_{A, k}, c_{B, k})$, the total arc length $S = \int_0^1 \|\mathbf{r}'(t)\|\,dt$ is computed. Vertices are resampled at equidistant arc-length intervals:

**Winding & Index Alignment**: Polygons are tested for clockwise vs. counter-clockwise orientation. If orientations disagree, vertex order is inverted. The starting vertex index is circularly shifted to minimize the total Euclidean displacement during the animation:
